transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been taking on too much. I keep starting things—work plans, certification schedules, stuff at home with the network, reaching out to old contacts—and I don’t really stop when I should. It gets intense enough that my wife or my director has to step in.
Have you had any periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable, where you were doing things more quickly or intensely than usual?

Yeah… I guess there are weeks where I feel kind of wired, like I can handle anything and I don’t want to slow down. And then if there’s some little delay, or my wife asks a question, I can get… sharper than I mean to. Like they’re getting in my way on purpose.
Have you ever had a time when your mood was so high or so irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self, even if others might not have understood why you were reacting that way?

Yeah… there are weeks where I feel almost… electric, I guess. Like I’m unstoppable. But then something small happens—a delay, or my wife asks me something—and I snap, like they’re slowing me down on purpose.
How long do these periods of feeling 'electric' or 'unstoppable' usually last, and have they ever caused problems at work or at home, or led to you needing less sleep than usual?

It’s been going on for… maybe a year and eight months, something like that. Those stretches where I’m really driven and don’t sleep much, and I feel more sure of myself than usual. I don’t really like admitting it, but yeah, it’s been around that long.
Can you describe a specific time when this 'electric' or 'unstoppable' feeling was noticeably different from how you usually feel, and how others around you reacted to it?

I mean… there was a week where I just felt really charged up, like I could push through anything. It didn’t feel like my normal self.

But then little things set me off. Like if something took too long, or my wife asked me a simple question, I’d snap at her. In my head it felt like people were trying to slow me down on purpose… even if I guess they probably weren’t.

Can you tell me if there have been specific periods — days or weeks — where your mood was clearly different from your usual self, and stayed that way most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a few days in a row?

Yeah… there are times like that. Usually it’s a stretch of days, sometimes most of a week, where I just feel… wired, like I can do anything. It’s there most of the day.

And then I get irritated fast. Like a tiny delay or my wife asking me something can make me snap, because in the moment it feels like people are trying to slow me down.
Can you recall a specific time when your mood was so high or irritable that it was clearly different from your usual self, and this lasted for several days in a row?

Yeah… I can think of times like that. Some weeks I feel almost… electric, like I’m unstoppable. It’s not really my normal mood.

But it can turn fast. If there’s some tiny delay, or my wife just asks me something, I snap. In the moment it feels like everyone’s trying to slow me down on purpose.
Can you think of a time when you felt this 'electric' or 'irritable' mood for at least 4 days in a row, where it was clearly different from your usual mood and affected how you acted most of the day?

Yeah… I think so. There’ve been weeks where for several days I felt kind of electric, like I could just keep going and nothing should get in my way.

And I’d be on edge most of the day. Even little stuff—like a delay, or my wife asking me something—could make me snap, like she was trying to slow me down.
Can you confirm if there was a specific time when you felt this 'electric' or 'irritable' mood for at least 4 full days in a row, without it going away for even a day in between?

Yeah… I think there were times it lasted that long. Like, several days in a row where I felt almost electric, like I was unstoppable.

It didn’t really let up, not for a full day. And I’d get irritated fast—little delays, or my wife asking me something, felt like people were slowing me down on purpose.

Can you think of a specific time when you felt this 'electric' or 'irritable' mood for at least 4 days straight, and during that time you also experienced other changes like needing less sleep, talking more quickly than usual, having racing thoughts, doing more tasks than usual, or taking risks you wouldn’t normally take?

Yeah… there was a stretch like that. I don’t remember the exact dates.

I just couldn’t stop starting things. Work plans, certification schedules, upgrades to the home network… even reaching out to old contacts. It felt like I had to keep pushing, and I’d blow past normal limits until my wife or my director had to step in.

Can you tell me if there was a time when, in addition to feeling electric or irritable, you also experienced at least a few of the following: needing much less sleep than usual, talking more quickly than normal, having thoughts race through your head, doing a lot more things than usual, or taking on risks you wouldn't normally take?

Yeah… the sleep part, definitely.

There’ve been runs where I’d sleep maybe three hours, then wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning feeling sharp. Not tired, really. More like… I’d been given extra time to use.
Can you tell me if there was a time when you felt this way — electric or irritable — for at least a full week straight, without a break, and it was clearly different from how you usually feel?

Yeah… I think so. Some weeks it’s like that, where I feel almost electric, like I can push through anything.

But I also get… irritated. Like even a small delay, or my wife asking me something, can make me snap because it feels like people are slowing me down on purpose. It’s not really my normal state.

Can you confirm if there was a time when you felt this 'electric' or 'irritable' mood for at least a full week, and during that time you were significantly increasing your work or other goal-directed activities nearly every day?

Yeah… I’d say so. That’s kind of why I came in.

I get into these stretches where I’m launching one thing after another — work plans, certification stuff, home network upgrades, messaging old contacts. It’s nearly every day, and I don’t really stop until my wife or my director tells me I’m pushing too far.

Can you confirm if there was a specific period lasting at least one week where your mood was clearly elevated or irritable, and during that time you were noticeably more active or restless compared to when you’re feeling normal?

Yeah. There was a stretch like that.

I wasn’t just in a better mood… I was moving all the time. I’d pace around the house with my laptop, mess with the garage, rewrite project boards over and over. If I tried to just sit and watch a show, I’d feel… uncomfortable, like I needed to get up and do something.

Can you confirm if there was a time when, during one of these 'electric' or irritable periods lasting at least a week, you also experienced at least two more changes like racing thoughts, talking faster than usual, or taking on more than you normally would?

Yeah… racing thoughts, definitely.

It’s like one idea opens ten more in my head. I’ll be typing an email, and before I finish the sentence I’m already three solutions ahead… then I kind of lose the original point. It’s hard to slow it down.
Can you confirm if there was a specific time when you felt this 'electric' or irritable mood every day for at least a full week without it letting up, even for a day?

Yeah… there have been weeks like that.

It’s not just a good mood. I feel almost electric, like I can’t be stopped. And if something small gets in the way — even my wife asking a question or some little delay — I snap, like people are slowing me down on purpose. It can go on day after day.

Can you confirm if there was a specific period lasting at least one week where your mood was clearly elevated or irritable, and during that time you were noticeably more active or restless nearly every day, to the point where it caused problems at work or at home?

Yeah… I mean, yes.

During those weeks I’m just… up and moving nearly every day. I’ll pace around the house with my laptop, reorganize the garage, redo project boards over and over. If I try to sit and watch TV, I feel physically uncomfortable, like I need to get back up.

It did cause problems at home. I know that.

Can you confirm if there was a specific time when your mood was clearly elevated or irritable for at least a week, and during that time you also experienced at least three of the following: needing much less sleep than usual, talking so fast others couldn’t keep up, thoughts racing through your head, getting distracted easily, doing a lot more things than usual, or taking on risky projects or behaviors you wouldn’t normally do?

The sleep part, yeah.

There have been runs where I’m only sleeping maybe three hours… waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning, wide awake. And it doesn’t feel like being tired. It feels like I’ve been given extra time or something.

The rest… I’d have to think about it, but that one definitely happens.

Can you confirm if, during one of these weeks when you felt electric or irritable, you also experienced at least two other changes like talking faster than usual, getting distracted easily, or taking on risky projects or behaviors you wouldn’t normally do?

Yeah… distractibility, definitely.

During those times, it’s like anything can pull me off track. My phone buzzes, or there’s a fan clicking, or someone walks past my office door, and I’m gone from whatever report or ticket I was supposed to be finishing. I’ll just abandon it without really deciding to.

Can you confirm if there was a specific time when your mood was clearly different from usual—either elevated or irritable—for at least a full week, and during that time it significantly affected how you functioned at work or at home?

Yes. There are weeks where I feel… almost electric, like I can’t really be stopped.

And then at home especially, if there’s some small delay or my wife asks me a simple question, I snap. It feels in the moment like people are slowing me down on purpose. So… yeah, it affects things.
